newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CEZ mulls extending N-plant's life.
newsitem.headline: Czech CEZ mulls extending N-plant's life.

text.p: Czech utility CEZ a.s. said on Tuesday it might prolong the life of its Dukovany nuclear power plant beyond its planned closure in 2015.

CEZ spokesman Ladislav Kriz said the 11-year-old Soviet-designed plant, currently the country's only nuclear power facility in operation, was in good condition and could stay open about 10 years longer than expected.
"We are preparing for it, the power plant is ready for it, and the investment done there is realised with the aim to prolong the operation," Kriz told Reuters.

He also said another reason to leave it open was due to the faster-than expected increase in domestic demand for electricity in recent years. Forecasts show the consumption boom continuing into next century.
Kriz added that the slower-than-expected degradation of Dukovany's four reactors had "been such that it suggests they could last longer."

CEZ would have to invest an extra 10 billion crowns ($366 million) into the station to keep it going, Kriz said, but stressed that no plan had yet been approved and much would depend on the government's future energy policy.

Dukovany, opened in 1985 about 200 km southeast of Prague, is equipped with four VVER-440 megawatt reactors, a later generation than RBMK reactors, one of which exploded at Chernobyl in Ukraine in 1986 in the world's worst nuclear plant disaster.
CEZ is building a 2000-megawatt atomic plant at Temilin south of Prague, which like Dukovany is near the Austrian border.
Construction on Temilin began in the mid-1980s, using even more modern Soviet-designed VVER-1000 reactors.
After the fall of communism in 1989, the Czech government approved a plan to upgrade the Temilin project with a control system supplied by U.S.-based Westinghouse Electric Corp..
The project has run into repeated delays.
CEZ's latest plan is for the first bloc to open in 1998.
Environmentalists and the neighbouring Austrian government have complained that the Czech nuclear power programme is dangerous and unnecessary.
